title: Borrowed but Not Implemented: Educational Policy Borrowing and the Implementation Gap in Centralized Systems
text_snippet: Borrowed but Not Implemented: Educational Policy Borrowing and the Implementation Gap in Centralized Systems ABSTRACT This study examines why borrowed educational reforms in Kuwait have failed. It is based on in‐depth interviews with 20 key figures from the Ministry of Education (MOE), including former Ministers, and administrators from the Kuwait National Center for Education Development (NCED). The study found prior research suggesting that the failures of Western education not being a suitable fit for Kuwait were incorrect, and that a weakness in following correct implementation patterns was the main reason. Borrowed reforms adoption without modification, top‐down implementation with a lack of ‘on‐the‐ground’ implementers' inputs, and insufficient alignment with the existing infrastructure and the local school culture, had led to fragmented educational reforms and on‐the‐ground resistance. The study recommends that reforms should include orientation and planning, collaboration with stakeholders, modification of the reforms to fit the local socio‐cultural context, and effective ongoing monitoring and tracking systems.

text_snippet: Learning in GenAI ‐Mediated Education: A Hybrid SEM – PNA Approach to English Majors' Smart Service Interactional Experience and Anxiety ABSTRACT Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has reshaped EFL learning, yet its extensive use has also produced distinctive anxieties. Few studies have examined how such anxiety emerges from the holistic interaction between learners and intelligent systems and fewer still have drawn pedagogical implications. Guided by Hassenzahl's Model of Pragmatic and Hedonic Quality of User Experience, we investigated how eight smart service interactional experience (SSIE) dimensions related to GenAI‐mediated EFL anxiety among 478 English majors across three Chinese universities. title: Making Innovation Learning Accountable: Intellectual Property Governance and Integrity‐Oriented Judgement in University‐Industry Collaboration
text_snippet: Making Innovation Learning Accountable: Intellectual Property Governance and Integrity‐Oriented Judgement in University‐Industry Collaboration ABSTRACT University‐industry collaboration has become a central way through which higher education seeks to make innovation learning authentic, applied and professionally relevant. Yet the very authenticity of such collaboration changes the institutional condition of learning. When students participate in externally connected projects, incubators, sponsored work, entrepreneurial programmes or technology‐transfer environments, their learning becomes entangled with ownership claims, disclosure rules, university resources, external interests and commercial possibilities. title: Tertiary English Education in the GenAI Era: Chinese English Majors' Cognitive Appraisals, Employment Anxiety, and Informal Digital Learning
text_snippet: Tertiary English Education in the GenAI Era: Chinese English Majors' Cognitive Appraisals, Employment Anxiety, and Informal Digital Learning ABSTRACT The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has intensified employment anxiety among Chinese English majors, posing new challenges for foreign language education and career development. However, how their cognitive appraisals of GenAI shape engagement in GenAI‐mediated informal digital learning of English (GenAI‐IDLE) remains underexplored. title: ‘You Care More if You Work Yourself to Death’: Exploited Altruism and Other Adverse Factors Affecting the Culture Within an English Higher Education Initial Teacher Training Team
text_snippet: ‘You Care More if You Work Yourself to Death’: Exploited Altruism and Other Adverse Factors Affecting the Culture Within an English Higher Education Initial Teacher Training Team ABSTRACT This paper shares the ways in which Higher Education Lecturers (HELs) in Initial Teacher Training (ITT) at an English university perceive their workplace culture. Data from 15 questionnaires and 12 semi‐structured interviews underwent thematic analysis. The findings suggest that culture was a preoccupation, with trust, relationships and idealism featuring as sub‐themes within that focus. The attitudes and perceptions underpinning the sub‐themes contributed towards a sense of altruism being exploited by systems and leadership structures. This appeared to be counter‐balanced through reliance upon upstairs/downstairs bonding and exclusions. Micro‐resistance was therefore apparent, but with little impact on improving the strategies and space of ITT. From this study, suggestions are therefore made for all stakeholders in ITT to reflect on their occupation of place, space, strategies and tactics, with an emphasis on developing compassionate leadership.

title: Shadow Education: Broadening and Deepening Research in the Field
text_snippet: Shadow Education: Broadening and Deepening Research in the Field ABSTRACT This Editorial frames a collection of 10 papers on private supplementary tutoring, which is widely known as shadow education. The Editorial has two main starting points. First is a predecessor collection published in the European Journal of Education in 2020; and second is a 2025 publication developed from a UNESCO Policy Forum. The Editorial also places this new collection in the context of wider literature to show advances in both broadening and deepening research on shadow education. Then, looking forward, it presents possible agendas for continuing research across individual, local, national, regional, and global contexts.

title: L2 Teachers' Work Engagement in AI‐Enhanced Teaching Environments: Harnessing a Phenomenological Approach to Uncover Its Personal and Contextual Determinants
text_snippet: L2 Teachers' Work Engagement in AI‐Enhanced Teaching Environments: Harnessing a Phenomenological Approach to Uncover Its Personal and Contextual Determinants ABSTRACT Adopting a descriptive phenomenological approach, this study sought to unravel the determinants of L2 teachers' work engagement within artificial intelligence (AI)‐assisted instructional contexts. To this end, 49 English language teachers were purposefully selected from Chinese educational contexts to complete an open‐ended questionnaire online. Data were thematically analysed using MAXQDA (v. 2024), revealing that teachers' work engagement has been shaped by specific personal traits— adaptability , AI literacy , self‐efficacy , resilience and emotional regulation —and contextual conditions, including leadership behaviours , professional development opportunities , colleague support and learner engagement . These findings highlight how these individual and environmental factors together have influenced teachers' ability to remain engaged while navigating AI‐mediated teaching demands. By uncovering these personal and contextual determinants, the study offers practical insights for educational leaders and policymakers seeking to support L2 teachers in effectively integrating AI tools into instruction.

title: ‘Pivotal but Not a Priority’: Exploring the Process and Affecting Factors of Undergraduate Thesis Writing in China
text_snippet: ‘Pivotal but Not a Priority’: Exploring the Process and Affecting Factors of Undergraduate Thesis Writing in China ABSTRACT Undergraduate thesis writing is widely regarded as a capstone of higher education. Yet most research has examined the quality of the finished thesis and has paid little attention to the writing process and the factors that shape it, especially in English‐as‐a‐foreign‐language (EFL) contexts. This study examined the process of undergraduate thesis writing and its influencing factors among English majors at one Chinese normal university. The data were analysed through descriptive statistics and thematic content analysis, with triangulation across sources. text_snippet: Education, Knowledge Communication and Sustainable Governance: An Analytical Framework for University Narratives and Digital Knowledge Infrastructures ABSTRACT Universities increasingly organise and communicate sustainability‐related knowledge through reports, databases, digital collections and other knowledge infrastructures. text_snippet: Chinese Doctoral Students' Conceptions of Research in Applied Linguistics: A Sociocultural Perspective ABSTRACT Although Conceptions of Research (CoR) fundamentally shape doctoral students' research practices, longitudinal understandings of how early‐stage doctoral students dynamically construct and develop their CoR remain scarce. Grounded in sociocultural theory (SCT), this qualitative case study examined the CoR development of two Chinese doctoral students in applied linguistics over one semester. Data from journals and interviews revealed that the students' CoR evolved across two intertwined dimensions: their conception of research's nature shifted from being perceived as formulaic, through demanding, to ultimately dialogic, while its purpose transitioned from personal interests, through publication‐oriented survival, toward a socially responsible practice. text_snippet: “The Wind Beneath Their Wings”: TPACK , Growth Mindset, Commitment, and Teachers' Motivation to Integrate Artificial Intelligence of Things ABSTRACT While prior research emphasizes teachers' technology integration for educational innovation, little is known about how three core elements, including technology (technological pedagogical content knowledge; TPACK), self (growth mindset; GM), and students (commitment to students' academic achievement; CSAA), jointly relate to motivation to adopt emerging technologies like Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT). title: ChatGPT in Education: Balancing Professional Autonomy, Transforming Relationships and Rethinking the Purpose of Education
text_snippet: ChatGPT in Education: Balancing Professional Autonomy, Transforming Relationships and Rethinking the Purpose of Education ABSTRACT Teachers must, in one way or another, address issues of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and generative AI (GAI). The urgency became even more acute when the chatbot ChatGPT was launched in November 2022, changing the conditions for teaching and learning in schools, creating tensions within the educational system. The aim of the study is to deepen understanding of teachers' experiences of how generative AI, specifically ChatGPT, shapes teaching and education in secondary and upper secondary schools. title: How Achievement Emotions and Grit Affect Learners' Psychological Well‐Being in AI ‐Based Language Education: A Bifactor Analysis
text_snippet: How Achievement Emotions and Grit Affect Learners' Psychological Well‐Being in AI ‐Based Language Education: A Bifactor Analysis ABSTRACT The presentation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within educational settings has changed the conventional learning settings to advanced tools that improve the students' academic achievement. Psychological Well‐being (PWB) is a critical element of students' achievement in AI‐based settings. In AI‐based language learning settings, achievement emotions and grit are specifically significant because they form the way students react to difficulties, engage with the learning activities and maintain motivation. title: Through the Teachers' Eyes—Primary School Teachers' Perceptions of Knowledge to Inform Their Practice
text_snippet: Through the Teachers' Eyes—Primary School Teachers' Perceptions of Knowledge to Inform Their Practice ABSTRACT This qualitative multiple case study examines teachers' perceptions of what knowledge they find useful, with our two cases being academically and non‐academically trained early‐career primary school teachers. Six teachers were interviewed to explore how different forms of knowledge influence their teaching practices. Findings indicated that while our two cases used a combination of sources to shape their practice, the academically trained teachers made more reference to scientific research. Non‐academically trained teachers expressed openness to scientific evidence, but struggled to engage with it due to lack of accessibility, practical challenges, and a tendency to prioritize experiential knowledge. Ultimately, both groups saw value in practical, immediately implementable knowledge that meets the specific needs of their classrooms.

title: Bridging Parental Investment and Children's Willingness to Communicate With AI : A Serial Mediation of Self‐Efficacy and Autonomy in AI ‐Enhanced Informal Digital Learning of English
text_snippet: Bridging Parental Investment and Children's Willingness to Communicate With AI : A Serial Mediation of Self‐Efficacy and Autonomy in AI ‐Enhanced Informal Digital Learning of English ABSTRACT In the context of AI‐empowered language education, informal digital learning of English has emerged as a key site for fostering young learners ' positive psycho‐emotional development. However, limited attention has been paid to how family factors shape children ' s willingness to communicate with AI. This study investigated how parental investment influences upper‐primary students ' willingness to communicate with AI in an AI‐enhanced informal digital learning of English context, focusing on the mediating roles of AI learning self‐efficacy and learning autonomy. Grounded in Social Cognitive Theory and Self‐Determination Theory, the study surveyed 659 upper‐primary students from eight primary schools. Results revealed a serial mediation pathway: parental investment → self‐efficacy → autonomy → willingness to communicate with AI. These findings extend parental investment research into AI‐enhanced informal digital learning of English contexts and integrate two major motivational frameworks into a unified model of child L2 psycho‐emotional functioning.

title: Exploring Teachers' Motivation for Sustainable Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in L2 Education: A Descriptive Qualitative Inquiry
text_snippet: Exploring Teachers' Motivation for Sustainable Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in L2 Education: A Descriptive Qualitative Inquiry ABSTRACT A growing body of research has indicated that using Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies offers different contributions to second/foreign language (L2) education. However, the intentions and motivations behind such adoption have received insufficient attention in the English as a foreign language (EFL) context. To fill the gap, this descriptive qualitative study employed an online focus group interview with 11 Chinese EFL teachers. The results of thematic analysis demonstrated five major themes regarding motivations and intentions for sustainable AI adoption. The teachers argued that they had sustainably used AI for ‘enhancing learners’ classroom engagement, ‘making learning personalised and adaptive for learners, delivering immediate and instant feedback to learners, ‘adding innovation and diversity to instruction’, and ‘staying updated and current with technology’. The findings highlight a need for providing professional development programmes for EFL teachers to raise their AI literacy and notify them of how their intentions mediate their AI‐driven practices.

title: Perceptions of School‐Based Health‐Preserving Practices and Health‐Related Learning Engagement Among Primary School Students in Kazakhstan
text_snippet: Perceptions of School‐Based Health‐Preserving Practices and Health‐Related Learning Engagement Among Primary School Students in Kazakhstan ABSTRACT The school period is critical for developing health‐related knowledge, attitudes and behaviours. However, evidence on primary school students' perceptions of school‐based health‐preserving practices and engagement with health‐related educational content remains limited in Kazakhstan. This cross‐sectional survey of 1750 primary school students aged 6–12 years in Kazakhstan assessed perceived health awareness, attitudes, perceived cognitive impact and health‐related learning engagement. title: The Impact of GenAI ‐Integrated Instruction on EFL Learners’ Willingness to Communicate, Motivation, and Well‐Being in Tertiary Education: A Mixed‐Effects Modelling Approach
text_snippet: The Impact of GenAI ‐Integrated Instruction on EFL Learners’ Willingness to Communicate, Motivation, and Well‐Being in Tertiary Education: A Mixed‐Effects Modelling Approach ABSTRACT Willingness to communicate (WTC) is recognised as a vital element in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning; however, developing students' WTC in tertiary education is usually a constant challenge. Likewise, improving students' well‐being and motivation is equally significant as these constructs support better engagement and successful language achievement among undergraduate students. Despite the quick incorporation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in education, there remains a critical research gap concerning the effect of GenAI‐supported instruction on the intersection of learners' well‐being, motivational states, and communicative behaviours. title: The Role of Multimodal AI Technology Integration in EFL Teachers' Turnover Intentions and Emotional Exhaustion: An Interventional Study
text_snippet: The Role of Multimodal AI Technology Integration in EFL Teachers' Turnover Intentions and Emotional Exhaustion: An Interventional Study ABSTRACT The role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies in different aspects of English as a foreign language (EFL) education has recently gained increasing attention. However, the contribution of multimodal AI tools to EFL teachers' reduction in their psycho‐emotional states and thoughts has remained under‐explored. To address the gap, this interventional study examined how the adoption of multimodal AI tools could decrease/prevent EFL teachers' turnover intentions and emotional exhaustion over two semesters. A sample of 157 Chinese EFL teachers in control ( N = 70) and experimental groups ( N = 87) filled in two online questionnaires at the start and end of the course. The results of ANCOVA revealed significant reductions in both constructs of teacher turnover intentions and emotional exhaustion after the intervention period. The study explains the contributions of the study to the theory and practice of multimodal AI technology integration into second/foreign language (L2) education, especially how such tools may regulate teachers' psycho‐emotional states over time.

title: Learners' and Teachers' Trust, Emotions, and Agency in AI‐Mediated Language Education
text_snippet: Learners' and Teachers' Trust, Emotions, and Agency in AI‐Mediated Language Education ABSTRACT The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms has reshaped feedback, assessment, and interactional practices. However, limited research has examined how learners' trust in AI systems relates to their emotional experiences and agency in AI‐mediated instruction. This study investigated the structural relationships among EFL translation learners' trust in AI‐assisted language feedback and assessment, foreign language enjoyment, foreign language classroom anxiety, learner autonomy, and perceived control. A cross‐sectional survey design was employed with 732 university EFL translation learners who had prior experience using AI‐supported language learning tools. Data were analysed through structural equation modelling (SEM) using AMOS. title: Resource Protection and Motivation: A Dual‐Path Moderated Mediation Model of the Impact of Perceived Organizational Change on Teachers' Work Engagement
text_snippet: Resource Protection and Motivation: A Dual‐Path Moderated Mediation Model of the Impact of Perceived Organizational Change on Teachers' Work Engagement ABSTRACT Although previous studies have established a positive correlation between perceived organizational change and teachers' work engagement, the underlying mechanisms and boundary conditions governing this relationship remain insufficiently explored. Integrating Event System Theory with Conservation of Resources Theory, this study develops a dual‐path moderated mediation model to examine how perceived organizational change influences teachers' work engagement through psychological contract violation and career resilience. Survey data were collected from 513 teachers across 15 vocational colleges in China using a two‐stage cluster convenience sampling approach. The empirical results indicate that rather than acting as a disruptive stressor, perceived organizational change functions as a positive structural event that significantly reduces psychological contract violation, thereby exerting a protective effect on work engagement. title: Resonance and Silence: English Teacher Agency in a Resource‐Constrained Professional Learning Community in China
text_snippet: Resonance and Silence: English Teacher Agency in a Resource‐Constrained Professional Learning Community in China ABSTRACT Professional Learning Communities (PLCs) are widely promoted for teacher learning and agency, yet their operation in resource‐constrained settings may reproduce institutional tensions. Using Cultural‐Historical Activity Theory, this 8‐month longitudinal case study of a Senior‐One English PLC in western Inner Mongolia, China, draws on 51 meeting recordings, reflective journals from one early‐career teacher, and interviews with eight PLC members to enable robust analysis of evolving interactions and agency over time. Teacher agency was shaped by multiple contradictions within the PLC, which were experienced differently across career stages. Teachers responded with varied strategies, including covert resistance, active coordination, rational adjustment, passive coping and silent compliance. The study proposes two exploratory constructs: efficacy compensation, where an early‐career teacher sought professional worth from self‐directed practice when collective recognition was unavailable; and institutional aphasia, the structural silencing of teacher voice under material scarcity, age hierarchy and top‐down administration. Practical implications for PLC design are discussed.

title: Augmented Reality in Early Childhood Education: Bibliometric Insights Into Global Trends and Thematic Clusters
text_snippet: Augmented Reality in Early Childhood Education: Bibliometric Insights Into Global Trends and Thematic Clusters ABSTRACT This study aims to conduct a bibliometric analysis of academic research on Augmented Reality (AR) technology in the field of preschool education. In the study, the distribution of publications according to years, countries, universities, authors, journals and keywords was analysed. Keywords were visualized using the VOSviewer bibliometric analysis software. The analysis revealed an increase in the number of publications over the past 3 years, with 2024 standing out as the year with the highest number of articles published. At the country level, Turkey demonstrated notable leadership in terms of the number of articles and citation rate. However, Greece, China, Slovakia and Spain were also identified as significant contributors to the field. title: When Professional Development Fails: EFL Academics Becoming Researchers Under Conditions of Institutional Stratification in Chinese Higher Education
text_snippet: When Professional Development Fails: EFL Academics Becoming Researchers Under Conditions of Institutional Stratification in Chinese Higher Education ABSTRACT Professional development is widely promoted as a strategy for enhancing the research capacity of EFL academics in higher education. However, existing research has paid less attention to the disciplinary knowledge and research practices through which research competence is developed. title: Modelling the Impact of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content ( AIGC ) on Critical Thinking and Emotional Learning: The Moderating Role of Intrinsic Motivation in Higher Education
text_snippet: Modelling the Impact of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content ( AIGC ) on Critical Thinking and Emotional Learning: The Moderating Role of Intrinsic Motivation in Higher Education ABSTRACT This study investigated the impact of Artificial Intelligence‐Generated Content (AIGC) tools, such as ChatGPT, on higher education students' intrinsic motivation, emotional learning, development of critical thinking and transformation of emotional learning. By designing a conceptual framework grounded in Self‐Determination Theory, the study explored how the use of AIGC tools shapes learning outcomes through both direct and moderating effects of intrinsic motivation. A quantitative cross‐sectional design was employed with 773 undergraduate EFL students from Chinese universities. title: Self‐Regulated Read‐To‐Write Strategies ( SR ‐ R2W ): Examining Its Structure, Antecedents, and Associations With Writing Performance
text_snippet: Self‐Regulated Read‐To‐Write Strategies ( SR ‐ R2W ): Examining Its Structure, Antecedents, and Associations With Writing Performance ABSTRACT Self‐regulated reading‐to‐write (SR‐R2W) refers to a process whereby proactive and strategic learners gain information effectively through reading to improve their writing. The present study focused on four types of strategies, including mining reading, cognitive strategies, recalling while writing, and peer revision reading. The impacts of strategy use on writing performance and the antecedents of strategy use were examined. The participants were 759 fourth‐ and fifth‐grade English learners in Hong Kong. Structural equation modelling (SEM) suggested that for both fourth‐ and fifth‐grade students, SR‐R2W strategy use had a significant positive relationship with writing performance. Self‐efficacy in reading and writing and interest in writing, two key motivational variables, were positively associated with students' SR‐R2W strategy use. This study sheds light on the contribution of SR‐R2W to English learners' writing, which has important implications for English writing instruction.

text_snippet: Unpacking English Language Teachers' Professional Learning Needs in the Age of AI : A Descriptive Qualitative Analysis of Perceptions, Expectations and Suggested Supports ABSTRACT Professional learning, a significant factor in teacher education, has received increasing attention across contexts and fields. text_snippet: Learners' Attitudes Towards Generative Artificial Intelligence, Technology Comfort and Intentions to Adopt AI Tools in Education ABSTRACT The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in music education and creative production has introduced new opportunities for music learners to compose, arrange and refine musical works through AI‐assisted technologies. text_snippet: Pre‐Service English Teachers’ Reported Roles and Practices in Promoting Self‐Regulated Learning During the K‐12 Practicum ABSTRACT This study examines pre‐service English teachers' reported roles and practices in promoting self‐regulated learning (SRL) in K–12 classroom contexts during their practicum, as well as the challenges they encounter. Adopting a multidimensional view of SRL encompassing cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, and behavioural strategies, the study involved three pre‐service English teachers undertaking their practicum in K–12 settings with prior teaching experience in either state or private schools. Data were collected through reflective journals, semi‐structured interviews, and focus group discussions and analysed thematically. The findings indicate that the participants demonstrated strong awareness of SRL and reported enacting a range of practices, including goal setting, motivational support, and time management, in their teaching. title: Agency in Academic Career Development Within Neoliberalism: Chinese as an Additional Language Teachers' Trajectories
text_snippet: Agency in Academic Career Development Within Neoliberalism: Chinese as an Additional Language Teachers' Trajectories ABSTRACT The pursuit of academic careers within neoliberal higher education is increasingly characterised as uncertain, insecure and fragmented. Previous studies have predominantly depicted the challenges and tensions experienced by language teachers in sustaining their career development. However, there remains a lack of research on how career agency (i.e., agentic actions and choices) is negotiated and exercised by individuals at the micro level. This multiple case study traces the career trajectories of a group of Chinese as an additional language (CAL) teachers, focusing on how they make decisions and enact actions to navigate their academic careers. The findings reveal diverse manifestations of career agency among the participants. Their career accounts indicate how different elements, such as neoliberal norms, personal values, professional status and career goals, intersect in their choices and actions as they navigate individual academic careers. title: Conceptualising Ideologically Bounded Equity in Japan: A Document Analysis of Curriculum Governance, High‐Stakes Transitions and Shadow Education
text_snippet: Conceptualising Ideologically Bounded Equity in Japan: A Document Analysis of Curriculum Governance, High‐Stakes Transitions and Shadow Education ABSTRACT This study examines how responsibility for educational fairness is represented across curriculum governance, reform cycles, selective transitions, supplementary education and values and moral education in Japan. It uses thematic document analysis of a criterion‐based purposive corpus of 43 documents: six Japanese official documents, five OECD publications and 32 academic or scholarly sources. The analysis identifies a substantive public guarantee of common curricular provision, meaningful but uneven recalibration across the Yutori and Post‐Yutori periods, socially differentiated conditions for converting provision into valued pathways and heterogeneous functions of shadow education. Values and moral education have substantive pedagogical and normative purposes, but the corpus does not show that they directly legitimise examination‐based inequality. title: Exploring the Link Between Distributed Leadership and Teacher Enthusiasm in a Centralized Education System: The Mediation of Teacher Growth Mindset and the Moderation of Supportive School Culture
text_snippet: Exploring the Link Between Distributed Leadership and Teacher Enthusiasm in a Centralized Education System: The Mediation of Teacher Growth Mindset and the Moderation of Supportive School Culture ABSTRACT This study aimed to test a multilevel moderated mediation model of distributed leadership's associations with teacher enthusiasm, with teacher growth mindset as the mediator and supportive school culture as the moderator. We employed data from 1056 Turkish teachers working in 96 basic and upper secondary schools and performed multilevel structural equation modelling with Bayesian estimation. Our findings revealed direct associations of distributed leadership with teacher enthusiasm and indirect associations via teacher growth mindset. text_snippet: Relational Work in Higher Education: University Staff Perspectives on Institutional Responsibility for Student Well‐Being ABSTRACT As concerns about student mental health have intensified, responsibility for supporting student well‐being is increasingly negotiated in everyday interactions between students and staff. This study aims to foreground the relational and caring dimensions of academic practice. It does so by examining how university staff understand and navigate their professional role in relational work to support students, and how this work is shaped by structural and emotional conditions. Drawing on five focus group interviews with 27 teaching and student‐support staff across multiple campuses and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, the study shows that care, trust, and accessibility are integral to everyday pedagogical and support practice. At the same time, relational engagement is weakly formalised and unevenly recognised, creating tensions around professional boundaries, workload, and emotional responsibility. The findings suggest that responsibility for student well‐being is channelled through everyday staff–student relationships within institutional frameworks that provide limited structural and institutional recognition.

However, its role may be constrained by the cognitive load generated when students navigate complex digital tools, resources, and learning tasks. This study, therefore, adopted an explanatory sequential mixed‐methods design to examine whether digital competence was associated with learners' engagement and whether cognitive load moderated this relationship. Quantitative data were collected from 339 Chinese university EFL learners through a questionnaire measuring digital competence, cognitive load and engagement. Regression analysis showed that cognitive load was negatively associated with engagement and significantly moderated the relationship between digital competence and engagement. text_snippet: Examination of Online Learning Strategies With Cluster Analysis ABSTRACT The aim of this study is to identify the learning strategies of students taking e‐courses in e‐learning environments using clustering algorithms, a data mining technique and to determine how these strategies are distributed according to the variables gender, class, faculty, computer and Internet usage level, and Internet usage time. The survey model was used in the study conducted in accordance with this objective. The study involved 518 students taking online courses at a university. The data obtained were analysed and interpreted using descriptive statistics and cluster analysis. text_snippet: Enjoyment and Engagement in AI ‐Mediated Informal Digital Learning of English: A Latent Growth Curve Modelling Study ABSTRACT Enjoyment and engagement are critical for effective language learning, yet little is known about how these experiences evolve over time in AI‐mediated informal digital English learning (IDLE). Previous studies have mainly relied on cross‐sectional designs, limiting understanding of the dynamic development of emotional and behavioural engagement. This study aims to examine the longitudinal trajectories of students' enjoyment and engagement in AI‐mediated IDLE and to identify factors influencing these changes. A total of 494 university students participated in a semester‐long study, completing three waves of surveys to capture changes in enjoyment and engagement. Latent growth curve modelling was used to estimate initial levels, growth trajectories, and the dynamic relationship between the two constructs. text_snippet: The Role of Perceived Teacher Fairness in EFL Students' Academic Outcome: Mediating Effects of Achievement Emotions on Engagement and Resilience ABSTRACT As two significant elements in education, resilience and engagement have been at the center of attention in the English as a Foreign Language (EFL) research, as they both influence learners' academic achievement and their psychological growth. Among different factors, teacher fairness has progressively been known as a vital interpersonal element forming students' motivational and emotional performance; however, its effect in foreign language teaching is overlooked. In EFL contexts, where students often experience heightened vulnerability due to linguistic and cultural barriers, the role of fairness becomes even more critical. Besides, considering the facilitative effect of positive emotions in the route of learning in line with Control‐Value Theory (CVT), the present research sought to investigate their mediating effect in the teacher fairness, engagement, and resilience relationship within EFL students in China. text_snippet: Student Engagement in AI ‐Supported Learning: Unpacking Psychological Drivers via Neural Network Analysis ABSTRACT As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in higher education, student engagement in AI‐supported learning has become an important indicator of learning quality and educational effectiveness. However, existing research has paid relatively limited attention to the psychological mechanisms through which students become actively involved in AI‐supported learning environments. Grounded in control‐value theory, this study examined the relationships among growth mindset, enjoyment, hope, pride, and engagement in AI‐supported learning among university students. A questionnaire survey was conducted with 563 students who had prior experience of AI‐supported learning. Structural equation modelling was used to test the hypothesized relationships and mediating effects, while artificial neural network analysis was further employed to examine nonlinear predictive importance. title: Gender Differences in Agentic Career Goals and the Choice of Field of Study
text_snippet: Gender Differences in Agentic Career Goals and the Choice of Field of Study ABSTRACT Women's representation in tertiary education has reached parity in many countries, although regional disparities persist. Furthermore, there is still significant horizontal gender segregation in some fields of study. Among other explanations, it is suggested that men and women might prioritise different life and career goals. Men are often perceived as preferring fields that offer higher earning potential and opportunities for leadership, while women prefer those offering greater social utility. Since fields of study differ in the perceived potential for agentic and communal goals, this might explain horizontal segregation. However, recent empirical evidence on this association presents ambiguous findings. This study contributes to the literature by examining how agentic career goals shape first‐year students' choice of field of study at the University of Milan ( N = 11,201), moving beyond the conventional dichotomy between STEM and the humanities. title: Moving Beyond ‘Cheap Labour’: A Bourdieusian Analysis of Career Experiences and Trajectories of Vocational College Graduates in China
text_snippet: Moving Beyond ‘Cheap Labour’: A Bourdieusian Analysis of Career Experiences and Trajectories of Vocational College Graduates in China ABSTRACT This paper investigates the college‐to‐work transition of vocational college graduates, who are typically viewed as a homogeneous disadvantaged group. Drawing on Bourdieu's theories, this two‐wave panel study interviewed 33 Chinese vocational college graduates about their initial labour‐market experiences during their first year after graduation. This study reveals the heterogeneity and dynamics of four transitional patterns: dwelled, diverted, shifting and stuck, based on graduates' different degrees of field‐habitus congruence and major‐occupation match. This transition typology challenges oversimplified, often deficit‐based discourses of vocational graduates by illustrating how they perceive and engage with jobs differently. We also observe the self‐reinforcing tendency of graduates' career trajectories. The study challenges the conceptualisation of ‘successful’ and ‘problematic’ transitions, as normally measured by major‐job match, and suggests providing more targeted academic and career support to vocational students at an earlier stage, well before graduates form fixed career patterns.

title: Understanding Chinese Students' Social Networks and Second Language Identity Construction During Study Abroad in the UK
text_snippet: Understanding Chinese Students' Social Networks and Second Language Identity Construction During Study Abroad in the UK ABSTRACT Second language (L2) identity has gained increasing attention for its role in shaping study abroad (SA) experiences, yet its relationship with social networks remains underexplored. Drawing on social network theory and L2 identity framework, this qualitative study examined the interplay of L2 identity construction and social networks among three Chinese students in UK universities. Data were collected through social network questionnaires, self‐portraits and semi‐structured interviews, and analysed through a combination of ego‐network analysis, multimodal analysis, and thematic analysis. Findings reported that participants developed homogeneous‐dense, heterogeneous‐sparse, and heterogeneous‐balanced networks, respectively. These network types were associated with variations in identity‐related L2 competence, linguistic self‐concept, and L2‐mediated personal development through access to linguistic, cultural and affective resources. title: Examining Chinese University Students' Engagement Through Academic Self‐Efficacy, Teacher‐Student Rapport, and Flourishing: A PLS ‐ SEM and fsQCA
text_snippet: Examining Chinese University Students' Engagement Through Academic Self‐Efficacy, Teacher‐Student Rapport, and Flourishing: A PLS ‐ SEM and fsQCA ABSTRACT Student engagement is an important indicator of learning quality in higher education, yet its personal, relational, and psychological mechanisms require further examination. Based on data from 469 Chinese undergraduate students, this study investigated the relationships among academic self‐efficacy, teacher‐student rapport, flourishing, and student engagement. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM) was used to examine direct and indirect relationships, while fuzzy‐set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) was used to identify configurations leading to high and low student engagement. The PLS‐SEM results showed that academic self‐efficacy, teacher‐student rapport, and flourishing all positively predicted student engagement. Teacher‐student rapport and flourishing also mediated the relationship between academic self‐efficacy and student engagement, and the serial mediation pathway was significant. title: Predictors of Self‐Regulated Learning in AI‐Supported Language Education: A Social Cognitive Theory Perspective
text_snippet: Predictors of Self‐Regulated Learning in AI‐Supported Language Education: A Social Cognitive Theory Perspective ABSTRACT Guided by Social Cognitive Theory, this study explored how language learning curiosity, perceived teacher support, and AI literacy predict learners' self‐regulated learning (SRL) in AI‐supported language education, with grit and flow as mediators. Data collected from 1022 Chinese undergraduate students were analysed using descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modelling with bootstrapped mediation analysis, and psychological network analysis via SPSS, AMOS, and R. The results showed that all three antecedent variables were positively associated with grit and flow, which in turn significantly mediated their influences on self‐regulated learning. Network analysis further revealed that self‐regulated learning was the most pivotal node among the six constructs. These findings suggest that effective AI‐supported language learning requires not only technological access, but also motivational, contextual, technological, and psychological resources to foster learners into agentic and self‐regulated language learners.

title: Contested Recognition: Schools' Binary‐Gendered Institutional Architecture and the Erasure of Trans, Intersex and Nonbinary Students
text_snippet: Contested Recognition: Schools' Binary‐Gendered Institutional Architecture and the Erasure of Trans, Intersex and Nonbinary Students ABSTRACT Although legal recognition and visibility of gender diversity have increased in Germany since 2019, schools still enforce binary gender norms, which excludes or marginalises trans, intersex and non‐binary (TIN) students. This article examines based on Grounded Theory analysis of interview data how gender diversity is simultaneously recognised and negated in everyday school practice in Germany: by (a) linguistic‐discursive practices and norms, (b) epistemic‐discursive content taught or omitted, (c) physical‐symbolic organisation of facilities and PE, alongside (d) teachers' role. These dimensions mutually reinforce non‐recognition, producing invisibility/hypervisibility, safety risks as well as reduced participation in education of TIN students. Finally, the article discusses necessary transformations required in schools to foster the inclusion of TIN students.

text_snippet: Teaching With AI , Engaging With Purpose: University Teachers' Work Engagement in AI ‐Supported Higher Education ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping higher education, requiring university teachers to adapt their pedagogical roles, technological competence, and professional engagement. Drawing on the Job Demands–Resources (JD‐R) model, this study examined how organizational support and AI literacy were associated with university teachers' work engagement in AI‐supported teaching, with professional identity, resilience, and self‐efficacy as mediating personal resources. A questionnaire survey was conducted among 1135 Chinese university teachers with experience in AI‐supported teaching. Data were analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM), mediation analysis, and network analysis. text_snippet: Investigating Metaverse Implications for Enhancing Interactive Learning in Higher Education: An Empirical Study ABSTRACT The broad concept of ‘metaverse’ encompasses all future digital items. title: Existential Constructions and Syntactic Complexity in Chinese EFL Writing: A Corpus‐Based Comparative Study With ChatGPT ‐Enhanced Analysis
text_snippet: Existential Constructions and Syntactic Complexity in Chinese EFL Writing: A Corpus‐Based Comparative Study With ChatGPT ‐Enhanced Analysis ABSTRACT Existential constructions (ECs) play an important role in academic writing by introducing new information, expressing epistemic stance and facilitating information flow. Examining how EFL learners use different EC types can offer valuable insights into their syntactic development and writing proficiency. Previous research, however, has focused mainly on EC acquisition independently, with limited attention to the relationship between constructional usage and sentence‐level syntactic complexity. The present study investigates Chinese EFL learners' use of ECs across three categories: presentational, epistemic/evidential and interrogative forms. A corpus‐based comparative analysis was conducted using four corpora, with ECs extracted via ChatGPT‐assisted annotation and subsequent manual classification. title: Emotional Labour in Shaping Pre‐Service Teachers' Well‐Being: A Case Study of Rural Practicum Journeys
text_snippet: Emotional Labour in Shaping Pre‐Service Teachers' Well‐Being: A Case Study of Rural Practicum Journeys ABSTRACT This study explores the emotional journeys of three pre‐service teachers during their rural teaching practicum in China, focusing on how emotional labour develops and shapes teacher well‐being. Using reflexive thematic analysis of three narrative cases, the study traces participants' emotional labour trajectories over time. The findings show that all three teachers initially engaged in genuine expression before shifting to surface acting in response to practicum tensions, with two subsequently developing deep acting, whereas one remained reliant on surface acting. These divergent trajectories emerged through guided reflection that fostered critical emotional reflexivity, which was enabled or constrained by structural and contextual conditions. By providing a process‐oriented account of emotional labour trajectories during practicum, the study contributed to a deeper understanding of how pre‐service teacher well‐being evolved and fluctuated over time and offered practical implications for teacher education and rural practicum support.

title: A Time‐Centred Perspective on Classroom‐Based Physical Activity
text_snippet: A Time‐Centred Perspective on Classroom‐Based Physical Activity ABSTRACT Schools are recognized as a key setting for preventing physical inactivity–related health issues early in life. Despite schools offering a rich set of opportunities to integrate physical activity (PA) without disadvantages for learning, those opportunities are often underutilized in ‘traditional’ educational environments where PA is primarily restricted to physical education classes, with children and adolescents typically remaining sedentary during academic lessons. However, there is a growing interest in how integrating PA in classrooms can benefit children's health and cognition. In this context, we propose a novel perspective for promoting classroom‐based PA by integrating established frameworks focusing on (i) time as a central element for school learning, (ii) the PA dose, type and context, and (iii) interrupting prolonged sitting with brief bouts of acute PA. This novel time‐centred perspective provides a conceptual foundation for advancing research practices on classroom‐based PA to enhance the translation of scientific evidence into effective, real‐world educational practices.

title: Intercultural Education in Chinese University EFL Classrooms: Intercultural Communication Competence Profiles and the Predictive Roles of Teacher–Student Rapport and Classroom Engagement
text_snippet: Intercultural Education in Chinese University EFL Classrooms: Intercultural Communication Competence Profiles and the Predictive Roles of Teacher–Student Rapport and Classroom Engagement ABSTRACT Intercultural communication competence (ICC) is increasingly regarded as an important goal of intercultural education in university EFL classrooms, where students are expected to engage with diverse perspectives and communicate across cultural boundaries. However, previous research has often examined ICC through variable‐centred approaches, paying limited attention to how different ICC dimensions combine within individual learners and how classroom conditions differentiate students' intercultural development. title: AI ‐Driven Instruction and Its Influence on EFL Learners' Self‐Efficacy, Self‐Regulation, and Grit
text_snippet: AI ‐Driven Instruction and Its Influence on EFL Learners' Self‐Efficacy, Self‐Regulation, and Grit ABSTRACT Incorporating AI into language education has shaped new opportunities to increase learners' psychological resources; however, evidence on how AI‐driven instruction influences key traits such as self‐efficacy, self‐regulation and grit remains limited. To address this gap, the present research examined the effect of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) teaching intervention on these constructs among English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners. To this end, 123 Chinese EFL learners were selected and assigned to experimental and control groups and received the same syllabus content within 10 weeks. The two groups received the same syllabus material, but the experimental group engaged with an AI Chabot that offered adaptive learning support, customized encouragement and immediate feedback. On the contrary, the control group received conventional teacher‐centred teaching through a traditional context. title: Influence of Audience, Performing Conditions and Mental Health on Music Performance Anxiety: A Mediated‐Moderated Model
text_snippet: Influence of Audience, Performing Conditions and Mental Health on Music Performance Anxiety: A Mediated‐Moderated Model ABSTRACT Music performance anxiety (MPA) is one of the prevalent issues for musicians' socio‐emotional well‐being. However, research is scarce on how different psychological aspects influence novice musicians' MPA. Following Folkman's cognitive appraisal theory, this study examines how audience reaction influences MPA, with the mediating role of music performing conditions (MPCs) and the moderating role of their mental health (MH) in live performances in the Chinese context. The research design of the current quantitative study was a cross‐sectional survey. Data were collected from 270 final‐year music students in Beijing using a questionnaire. title: Seeing Sustainability: Aesthetic Public Pedagogy and the Formation of Ecological Citizenship
text_snippet: Seeing Sustainability: Aesthetic Public Pedagogy and the Formation of Ecological Citizenship ABSTRACT Ecological citizenship education has specified responsibility, agency, justice and participation, but it has not fully explained how citizens are formed through visual culture beyond formal education. This conceptual article develops aesthetic public pedagogy as a specific mode of public pedagogy: the contested process through which publicly circulating visual and sensory forms configure ecological relations and invite audiences into ecological subject positions. title: Exploring the Development of EFL Teachers' Resilience in China: A Bioecological Theory Perspective
text_snippet: Exploring the Development of EFL Teachers' Resilience in China: A Bioecological Theory Perspective ABSTRACT Against the backdrop of intense exam pressure and English curriculum reforms, EFL teachers face persistent occupational strains, yet existing research lacks sufficient insights into the dynamic formation mechanism of teacher resilience. Grounded in the bioecological theory, this study adopted semi‐structured interviews with five senior high EFL teachers to unpack the development of teacher resilience. Findings identify four core dimensions of EFL teachers' resilience amid occupational challenges, namely professional, emotional, social, and cultural resilience. Furthermore, proximal processes, personal characteristics, multi‐layered ecological contexts, and chronosystem interact synergistically to shape EFL teachers' resilience through reciprocal person‐environment transactions. This study expands the theoretical perspective for language teacher resilience research and offers practical implications to facilitate teachers' sustainable professional adaptation and wellbeing.

title: Exploring the Roots and Remedies of Students' Academic Hatred and Boredom in English Language Education: A Descriptive Qualitative Study
text_snippet: Exploring the Roots and Remedies of Students' Academic Hatred and Boredom in English Language Education: A Descriptive Qualitative Study ABSTRACT This study adopted a descriptive qualitative approach to explore the roots and remedies of Chinese EFL students' academic hatred and boredom. To this end, a sample of 43 Chinese EFL students was selected through convenience sampling for in‐depth interviews. Thematic analysis indicated that academic hatred stemmed from ‘language complexity,’ ‘instructional monotony,’ ‘excessive pressure’, and ‘examinations.’ The analysis further revealed that student boredom was primarily rooted in ‘lack of diversity’, ‘task difficulty’, ‘teacher instruction’, and ‘boring textbooks’. title: Factors Predicting Pre‐Service Teachers' Intentions to Use Artificial Intelligence Software
text_snippet: Factors Predicting Pre‐Service Teachers' Intentions to Use Artificial Intelligence Software ABSTRACT This research investigates the factors affecting pre‐service teachers' (PSTs) behavioural intentions (BI) to use artificial intelligence software in their future classes. The study examined factors affecting PSTs' behavioural intentions using an extended UTAUT framework comprising Performance Expectancy (PE), Effort Expectancy (EE), Social Influence (SI), Facilitating Conditions (FC), and Hedonic Motivation (HM). The study included 432 PSTs from the Faculty of Education at a state university in Eastern Türkiye. “Pre‐service Teachers' Acceptance Scale for AI‐Supported Education”, a valid and reliable scale, was used for data collection. The data were analysed using multiple linear regression. The results revealed that PE, SI, and HM were significant predictors of PSTs' BI, whereas EE and FC were not significant predictors. title: Policy Alignment, Institutional Strategies, and Collaboration Effectiveness in Sino‐Foreign Higher Education Collaboration: A PLS ‐ SEM Analysis
text_snippet: Policy Alignment, Institutional Strategies, and Collaboration Effectiveness in Sino‐Foreign Higher Education Collaboration: A PLS ‐ SEM Analysis ABSTRACT The Internationalization of higher education has recently led to a rapid growth of Sino‐Foreign University collaboration, but research so far has focused mostly on the factors of policy alignment ( PA ) and institutional strategies ( IS ) separately as predictors of collaboration effectiveness ( CE ). title: Validation of the Classroom Assessment Scoring System in Inclusive Upper Elementary Classrooms in Switzerland
text_snippet: Validation of the Classroom Assessment Scoring System in Inclusive Upper Elementary Classrooms in Switzerland ABSTRACT A high interaction quality is the cornerstone for successful academic and socio‐emotional development in children. The Classroom Assessment Scoring System (CLASS) is a reliable and valid tool to develop high‐quality interactions in regular classrooms across cultures. The current paper aimed to study and to extend the reliability and validity of the CLASS‐Upper Elementary version (CLASS‐UE) to inclusive upper elementary classrooms in Switzerland, using data of co‐teaching teams from 64 Grade 3–6 classrooms across 14 cantons. Results showed good to excellent interrater reliability (IRR) across different measures for IRR. Furthermore, a multi‐level confirmatory factor analysis indicated a good fit of the theoretically proposed three‐factor structure, with some modifications (e.g., cross‐loading). These results are promising with regard to developing interaction quality in inclusive classrooms.
